rv.q: Kubrickian is the current don't-miss production at The Factory Theater.
'Kubrickian' proves why the company has lasting power, and I left the theater vowing to see the work of this company on a more regular basis.
In three plays and one year, Peercy has become a playwright I want to follow, wherever he takes me next.
The stellar performances and thought-provoking script alone make Kubrickian a play worth seeing.
'Kubrickian' isn't a polished work of theater, but to its credit it does capture the strange, disorienting feeling of the present moment and offers us a tantalizing hint of hope.
To me, Kubrickian is a niche audience kind of show.
As a totality, it is rather immature and amateurish and needs work. Its overall purposelessness doesn't rise to the level of being existential.
